commitments.provenance: current custody, review, transaction, and completion contracts
commitments.statement: Delivery retains one-writer custody, dirty-byte preservation, reviewed-commit authority, independent review, atomic transaction recovery, provider-observed completion, and per-Change failure isolation while resilience behavior changes.
Deterministic evidence-preserving recovery is engine-owned; repository reasoning remains reviewed Builder work; materially different outcomes produce one bounded user proposal.
Automatic convergence uses explicit idempotent-intent policy and durable operation fingerprints rather than transport retry_safe metadata.
The change evolves the current proven core through additive hardening and an intention facade before removing public low-level operations.
Interface cutover migrates no active claims, attempts, frontier positions, repair state, or compatibility schemas; active Changes finish or are explicitly abandoned first.

commitments.provenance: user request and current architecture evidence
commitments.statement: Storage technology and host topology remain unchanged unless focused proof identifies a residual correctness or operability problem that the current mechanisms cannot solve.

acceptance: Given a claim past its timeout whose worker termination is not established, acquisition retains custody and emits one bounded recovery action without resetting or relaunching the Change worktree.

Given an established-dead Builder claim with changed files, recovery creates isolated preservation evidence, restores the reviewed worktree boundary, releases custody, and permits successor acquisition.
Given repeated matching worker or provider failures, persisted retry policy reaches bounded attention instead of starting an unbounded fresh-worker or provider loop.
outcomes.promise: Delivery restores progress after worker failure without resetting a worktree beneath a potentially live writer and without losing dirty bytes.
outcomes.title: Fenced execution recovery

acceptance: Given the shared repair prompt, VS Code selects a named repair coordinator whose declared tools cover the current repair workflow and whose mutations remain Delivery-owned.
Given repair evidence with one safe route, the coordinator applies that route and reports the observed successor state without asking the user to select low-level operations.
Given materially different preservation, adoption, or discard outcomes, the coordinator presents one bounded question and applies only the selected engine-owned proposal.
Given repair requiring source edits or merge reasoning, Delivery issues a scoped Builder repair launch with normal exact-commit review before ordinary orchestration resumes.
outcomes.promise: One repair coordinator diagnoses current Delivery attention, applies engine-owned safe convergence, obtains one material user answer when needed, delegates reviewed repository repair, and returns control to orchestration.
outcomes.title: Coherent repair ownership

acceptance: Given a persistently failing checkpoint provider, reconciliation records attempt count, last failure, and next retry while bounded backoff prevents a fixed five-second retry storm.
Given Cockpit and MCP hosts against one workspace, shared reconciliation ownership prevents overlapping mutation while host restart permits pending work to continue.
Given a healthy pending checkpoint or acceptance observation, convergence proceeds without requiring the browser page to remain visible.
outcomes.promise: Checkpoint, publication, and acceptance reconciliation retry with bounded backoff, visible health, and no duplicate mutation ownership across concurrent hosts.
outcomes.title: Bounded background convergence

acceptance: Given one current Change, the public read projection supplies its semantic state, next action, repair proposal, and evidence links without requiring callers to join separate operator, health, Integration, and finalization views.

Given a Planner, Builder, Finalizer, or repair launch, one claim-bound submission contract records an identical replay once and rejects a different replay without exposing internal publication tokens.
Given current repair attention, one high-level repair request either converges safely, returns a reviewed repair launch, returns one version-bound proposal, or quarantines the affected Change.
Given the additive facade, maintained parity tests demonstrate the retained normal and repair behaviors before low-level MCP operations are removed from caller grants.
outcomes.promise: Routine callers express Design, action, result, answer, and repair intentions without sequencing internal heads, receipts, operation identifiers, or cleanup variants.
outcomes.title: Intention-oriented Delivery interface

acceptance: Given a quiescent cutover inventory, active Changes are completed or explicitly abandoned and no claim, attempt, frontier position, repair record, or compatibility schema is migrated.
Given the new caller surfaces, retired low-level MCP operations and repair choreography are absent from active agents, skills, prompts, HTTP routes, and generated operation registries.

Given a fresh canary Change, Design through provider-observed completion succeeds using the intention interface and injected worker, publication, restart, and repair failures converge through the retained guarantees.

Given fresh-clone recovery proof for admitted authority and review permission, remote snapshot machinery is retained, simplified, or removed according to that demonstrated contract rather than interface-count preference.
outcomes.promise: MCP, Cockpit, and shared agents use the intention interface while proven internal primitives remain private or are deleted only when their behavior is subsumed.
outcomes.title: Clean interface cutover

acceptance_observations: Given a timed-out Planner claim, acquisition returns termination-unconfirmed failure evidence while the frontier claim remains active.
Given a timed-out Builder claim, acquisition leaves writer custody, branch head, worktree bytes, and active claim unchanged.
Given another ready Change and available execution capacity, acquisition returns its launch while the timed-out Change remains occupied.
Given confirmed dispatch termination followed by direct recover_claim, dirty bytes are preserved and successor acquisition becomes available.
constraints: Use one stable termination-unconfirmed failure code with change, outcome, attempt, and claim identity.
Timeout is suspicion only; do not add heartbeat, daemon, lease storage, process killing, or schema migration.
Keep direct recover_claim semantics and dirty-worktree quarantine behavior unchanged.
Keep unrelated Changes acquirable when execution capacity remains.
proof_boundaries: Real PortfolioApplication, DeliveryRuntime, PortfolioCoordinator, and ChangeWorkspaceManager fixtures exercise acquisition and recovery.
required_outputs: Focused acquisition and explicit-recovery regression tests
tasks.result: Delivery acquisition reports timed-out Planner and Builder claims as termination-unconfirmed failures without resetting worktrees, releasing custody, or relaunching those Changes; direct confirmed recovery retains current preservation and restart behavior.
tasks.title: Retain expired claims pending termination confirmation

acceptance_observations: Given an acquisition failure with the termination-unconfirmed code and claim identities, Orchestrator reports bounded attention without invoking recover_claim.
Given a Builder dispatch_failure or terminated child invocation, Orchestrator calls recover_claim with the launch identities.
Given active customization validation, the timeout and dispatch-failure routes remain distinguishable.
constraints: Name the termination-unconfirmed code literally and preserve unchanged claim identity in reporting.
Do not grant Orchestrator Git, worktree mutation, or low-level repair authority.
Continue exact recover_claim after a dispatched child invocation terminates without a usable result.
proof_boundaries: Shared agent and workflow validators inspect the active Orchestrator contract; Delivery behavior remains covered by TASK-001.
required_outputs: Updated Orchestrator workflow and role boundary
Agent ecosystem regression coverage for timeout versus dispatch-failure recovery
tasks.result: Orchestration treats the termination-unconfirmed acquisition code as bounded attention and does not call recover_claim, while dispatch failures from completed child invocations retain the existing exact recovery route.
tasks.title: Route termination-unconfirmed attention without recovery

acceptance_observations: Given repeated matching provider failures, persisted attempt evidence produces increasing bounded delay and terminal attention at the configured budget.
Given distinct failure fingerprints, their retry budgets remain independent.
Given successful convergence after failures, the matching retry evidence no longer blocks eligibility.
Given process restart, retry evidence and next eligibility remain effective.
Given one failing Change, an independent ready Change remains serviceable.
constraints: Reuse current pending-checkpoint attempt evidence where it already owns the behavior.
Do not create a second generic retry state machine or use transport retry_safe as policy authority.
Keep per-Change failures isolated so sibling Changes remain serviceable.
Do not make semantic choices or perform destructive repair through retry policy.
proof_boundaries: Persisted Delivery runtime, PortfolioApplication, and DeliveryCheckpointSupervisor behavior are exercised across restart with provider dependencies replaced below the application boundary.
required_outputs: Retry policy integrated with current pending-checkpoint and recovery evidence
Focused restart, backoff, sibling-progress, and success-reset tests
tasks.result: Repeated matching worker-recovery and checkpoint-provider failures use stable fingerprints and persisted retry evidence to reach bounded attention with next-action guidance; successful convergence clears or supersedes its matching retry evidence.
tasks.title: Persist bounded repeated-failure convergence
